unresolved_added: The Summary reports a complete HCN, budget, occupancy, and promotion story, but every headline result remains internal to an uncalibrated simulation.
Related Work visibly retains [NOT good...], an ellipsis, (??), and an unfinished final clause; these draft remnants are excluded from positive language evidence.
The paper reconstructs personnel relations from limited information and reuses closeness notation before specifying disconnected-node handling or observed assignments.
Salary is treated as ability, equality/uniformity scales are not defined, and signed objective weights are chosen after unspecified random experiments.
The Genetic Algorithm uses 500 random initial solutions but reports no seed, population operators, stopping criterion, optimum gap, or comparison with the mentioned Tabu Search.
The personnel edge rule leaves sigma undefined, mixes three relationship conditions, and supplies no empirical tie-strength validation.
The organizational graph adds an artificial sink for LeaderRank, but the LeaderRank recurrence, initialization, damping, sink handling, and convergence trace are absent.
The revised RA similarity and logistic decay are not calibrated; beta, departure-time indexing, direct-neighbor behavior, and similarity normalization are under-specified.
Closeness and LeaderRank are combined by an inverse product without a disconnected-component policy, scale check, or empirical link to turnover.
The AHP judgment matrix is not strictly reciprocal, the text calls the score Equation (4) although it is labeled (2), and the reported CI/CR cannot substitute for a released calculation.

Employee efficiency is said to be inversely proportional to turnover intention but is not defined; cost units and provenance are missing, and the training-cost explanation mistakenly says recruiting costs.
The Poisson paragraph omits the promised monthly parameter statement, does not report seeds or fit evidence, and leaves the new-worker link reconstruction ambiguous.
The truncated-Gaussian promotion model clips service time and omits Administrative Clerks and Senior Managers without validating the distribution, interval widths, or eligibility consequences.
Figures 5-7 show one simulation path with no replications, uncertainty bands, raw series, or observed productivity outcome; the 9.8% reduction is therefore scenario-specific.
The budget uses sigma as a cost scale while later sensitivity uses sigma as a distribution parameter; source costs, units, seeds, and forecast error are not supplied.
The text says 25% and 35% churn cannot sustain 80% staffing, but the plotted 18% path also ends well below 80% of 370, so the decision boundary is internally unclear.
Tables 3 and 4 repeat exactly the same four output rows and values under sigma and mu, and the mu headers remain l, 2l, 3l; the second sensitivity claim is not independently supported.
The multiplex and HR extensions are illustrative: hometown ties, evaluation dimensions, vector scaling, Euclidean suitability, clustering interpretation, and fairness are not validated.
The final strengths infer rationality and correctness from common sense, while the explicit weaknesses admit grouped personnel categories and common-sense parameters caused by few data.
